title: Longest Cable Run in a Tree Network
statement:
A network of n devices, numbered 0 to n − 1, is wired as a tree: edges holds the n − 1 cables, each [a, b] joining two devices both ways. There are no loops and every device is reachable.

Return the number of cables on the longest path between any two devices. n is edges.length + 1, so an empty list means one device and the answer 0.

examples.why: 3 – 2 – 1 – 4 – 5 – 6. It does not pass through device 0, so measuring the depth below 0 gives only 4.
A single device has no cables.

hints: Try a BFS from one device. The device it reaches last is the farthest from the start. Is it special in some way?
In a tree, the farthest device from any starting point is always one end of some longest path.
So BFS from any device to find the farthest one, then BFS again from that device. The largest distance in the second BFS is the answer.

explain.intuition:
The brute force runs a BFS from every device and takes the largest distance seen, which is O(n²). The classic shortcut needs only two searches. Start anywhere, say device 0, and find the device a farthest from it. In a tree, a is always an endpoint of some longest path: if a longer path avoided it, you could reroute part of that path towards a and get something even longer.

Then the farthest device from a, found with a second BFS, is the other end, and its distance is the answer. Use iterative BFS rather than recursion: a path-like tree with 100 000 nodes overflows the call stack.
steps: Build an adjacency list for the n = edges.length + 1 devices.
BFS from 0, recording distances. Let a be the device with the largest distance.
BFS from a. Return the largest distance found.
pitfalls: Returning the height of the tree when rooted at 0. The longest path may not pass through the root, as in the second example.
Recursive DFS on a long chain: deep recursion overflows the stack in both JavaScript and Python.
Counting devices on the path instead of cables, which is off by one.

solutions.title: BFS from every device
solutions.idea: The longest path starts somewhere, so try every start and keep the largest distance.

solutions.title: Two BFS passes
solutions.idea: The farthest device from any start is one end of a longest path; BFS again from it.

solutions.title: Peel leaves layer by layer
solutions.idea: Repeatedly remove all current leaves. Each full round shortens the longest path by 2; the leftover 1 or 2 centre devices decide the parity.

followups: Cables now have lengths. Does the two-pass trick still work? (Yes, with weighted distances, as long as lengths are non-negative.)
Return a device in the middle of the longest path: the best place for a central server.
